text_blocks.snippet: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is often triggered by an infection, either viral or bacterial, though the exact cause is unknown. It's not contagious or inherited. Infections like Campylobacter jejuni, influenza, and cytomegalovirus are frequently linked to GBS. While vaccinations, including the flu vaccine, have been associated with a small risk, the connection is still being researched.
snippet_highlighted_words: an infection, either viral or bacterial, though the exact cause is unknown

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: GBS often follows an infection, with up to 70% of cases reporting an antecedent illness.
Campylobacter jejuni: A common bacterial cause, especially after gastrointestinal infections.
Viral infections: Influenza, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and Zika virus are also associated with GBS.

list.title: Vaccinations:
list.snippet: A small risk exists for GBS following certain vaccinations, including influenza and the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine, but the risk is very low compared to the risk from the illnesses themselves.

list.title: Other factors:
list.snippet: Surgery, trauma, and pregnancy have been reported as potential triggers, but these associations are not as well-established.

list.title: Autoimmune response:
list.snippet: GBS is an autoimmune disorder where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks the peripheral nerves. This attack can be triggered by the infections mentioned above.

text_blocks.snippet: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rare neurological disorder that has been reported following both COVID-19 infection and vaccination. While COVID-19 vaccines are generally safe and effective, and neurological side effects are rare, GBS has been identified as a potential, albeit uncommon, adverse event. Further research is needed to fully understand the incidence and causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and GBS.

list.title: GBS and COVID-19:
list.snippet: GBS can occur following both COVID-19 infection and vaccination.

list.title: Vaccine Safety:
list.snippet: COVID-19 vaccines have been shown to be highly effective and generally safe in large clinical trials.

list.title: Rare Neurological Side Effects:
list.snippet: Like all vaccines, COVID-19 vaccines can cause side effects, some of which are neurological.

list.title: GBS as a Potential Side Effect:
list.snippet: GBS is one of the rare neurological side effects that has been reported after COVID-19 vaccination, according to a National Institutes of Health (NIH) article.

list.title: Need for Further Research:
list.snippet: The exact frequency of GBS following vaccination is still being investigated, and more research is needed to understand the connection between vaccination and GBS development.

list.title: Monitoring and Evaluation:
list.snippet: The CDC and FDA are actively monitoring reports of GBS after COVID-19 vaccination.
